seoTitle: How to Export Airtable to Google Sheets Easily
metaDescription: Export Airtable records to Google Sheets using a manual CSV download or a live automated sync so your reporting spreadsheet stays current.
intro: Whether you need a one-time export or an ongoing live connection, moving data from Airtable into Google Sheets is possible with a couple of different approaches. This guide covers the quick CSV download method as well as setting up automated syncing so your spreadsheet updates whenever a record changes.

steps.heading: Check your view filters
steps.body: In Airtable, review your grid view filters and hidden columns to make sure you're exporting the right data.

steps.heading: Export to CSV
steps.body: Download your compiled table records as a clean CSV file.

steps.heading: Import into Google Sheets
steps.body: Upload and format the CSV dataset inside a blank Google Sheets file.

steps.heading: Set up automation, if needed
steps.body: For live syncing, use a no-code automation tool and authenticate with your Airtable personal access token.

steps.heading: Connect your Airtable base
steps.body: Link the specific Airtable base as a data source and set Google Sheets as the destination file.

steps.heading: Test the sync
steps.body: Run a live sync test to verify records transfer correctly, and check how linked records or media attachments are handled.

faq.question: What's the fastest way to do a one-time export?
faq.answer: Downloading your Airtable records as a CSV file and importing it into Google Sheets is the quickest manual approach.

faq.question: Can I keep my Google Sheet updated automatically?
faq.answer: Yes, using a no-code automation tool with a personal access token, you can set up a live sync that updates the spreadsheet whenever records change.

faq.question: What happens to linked records or attachments during export?
faq.answer: Linked records and media attachment links need special handling during export, since they don't always translate directly into simple spreadsheet cells.

faq.question: Do I need a developer to set up the live sync?
faq.answer: No, the process relies on no-code integration tools and a personal access token rather than custom development work.
